newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Truckers strike at Colombia's main Pacific port.
newsitem.headline: Truckers strike at Colombia's main Pacific port.

text.p: Truck drivers' of Colombia's main transport union declared a strike at the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura in protest at low freight rates, a union official said Monday.
The action began late Saturday but went largely unnoticed given that it came on a three-day bank holiday weekend which includes Monday.
Sources at the port, which handles about 60 percent of all Colombia's incoming and outbound foreign trade, including key coffee exports, said operations were not affected.
Officials of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), however, contested those claims, saying that nothing was being on- or off-loaded to trucks at the port, including coffee and sugar.

"The strike is affecting about 3,000 trucks in and around Buenaventura. Nothing is being loaded and those trucks that arrive with loads are being sent to wait in truck parks," local ACC representative Mario Antonio Umana told Reuters by phone.

He said the strike was declared because transport companies were refusing to honor a national accord, signed after a strike in April, to raise freight rates. Truck drivers saw their overheads rise even further last week when the government hiked fuel prices eight percent.

The ACC has called for government officials to take part in talks in Buenaventura and force transport company owners to pay the agreed rate of 42,700 ($39) per tonne of cargo between Buenaventura and Bogota. Umana said transport companies were currently paying less than 38,000 pesos ($34) per tonne.
No talks with government representatives have yet been arranged.

The ACC, which represents about 85 percent of truck drivers nationally, held nationwide strikes in October last year and April this year and virtually paralyzed all road freight. Dock workers also staged a crippling strike at Buenaventura earlier this year.

Other passenger and cargo transport companies are planning a possible strike Wednesday in protest at the hike in fuel costs, local radio reported. Umana said he did not yet know if the ACC would join.
